title: Warmth, blankets, and pressure-sore vigilance when skin changes

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: Hands, feet, or skin become cold, mottled, patchy, pale, grey, blue, purple, or otherwise changed; witnesses reach for blankets while carers watch comfort, dignity, and skin integrity.
ordinary_language_queries: mottled skin dying what to do
skin color changes end of life

content_layers.observation_text: Public sources describe coldness, mottling, and skin colour changes near death; practice language must pair warmth/comfort with pressure, fragility, and skin-tone accuracy boundaries.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Hospice UK, NHS-oriented sources, and Marie Curie support a skin-change record but do not by themselves settle how to describe all skin tones or how to manage pressure injury risk in a given setting.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record begins the body-description standard: what witnesses see should be named without making one skin tone the norm or treating the body as a spectacle.

what_this_is_not: not a prognosis from mottling alone
not a reason to overheat, reposition, or handle a fragile person without guidance
uncertainties: Skin changes look different across skin tones and lighting.
Pressure, heat, equipment, wounds, and frailty require local care guidance.
Future records need care-aide and nurse testimony about what “comfort” means physically.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should explain that coldness and colour changes can happen while encouraging care-team contact for comfort, wounds, or uncertainty.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect respectful colour vocabulary, blanket/temperature scripts, and the difference between comfort positioning and pressure care.
language_notes: Avoid white-skin defaults like “blue lips” without alternatives.
Use “patchy,” “mottled,” “dusky,” or “changed” only with source and skin-tone review.
Do not write body changes as horror.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
